profile.paceGuidance: Medically sustainable pace is ~0.5-1kg/week (~6-12kg over 3 months). Agreed approach: prioritise a deficit that doesn't rebound over hitting 20kg by a fixed date — decisive, visible progress by mid-December without the yo-yo pattern from past attempts.
profile.recoveryNote: Post kidney-stone surgery (uteroscopy + stent) — gentle walking + hydration only through October 2026. No gym/trainer/heavy exercise until doctor clearance at the mid-November follow-up with Dr Anupama.

howItAddsUp.note: Walk or short bus — walking it fully counts toward the target.

tips: Commute days (Mon/Tue/Wed/Fri) naturally give you a big chunk of the 15k just from Archway↔Canary Wharf↔Highgate — the gap to close is usually the PM Highgate-to-home leg and lunchtime movement.

On your WFH day (Thursday) there's no commute step floor, so that's the day most likely to fall short — schedule the 30-min walk/bike block in the morning deliberately rather than leaving it to chance.
Getting off one stop early on the Canary Wharf leg (either direction) is an easy, low-commitment way to add 1,500-2,000 steps without adding a dedicated session.
A short 10-15 min loop after getting off at Highgate station (before going straight home) is the single easiest lever if you're short for the day — flat, no extra planning, no kit needed.

spinalYoga.title: Spinal Yoga — Jindal-informed asana list
spinalYoga.intro: Cross-checked against Grade 1 L5-S1 spondylolisthesis: avoid deep forward spinal flexion, heavy loaded twisting and full backbends; favour core stabilisation and gentle, supported movement. Jindal's own spinal-disorder sheet already marked some poses as crossed-out or half-only — those calls are kept here rather than overridden.

safeAsanas.name: Marjariasana-Bitilasana (Cat-Cow)
safeAsanas.note: Gentle spinal mobility, well tolerated with spondylolisthesis.

safeAsanas.name: Setu Bandhasana, supported/gentle (Bridge)
safeAsanas.note: Strengthens glutes/posterior chain without loaded flexion — keep it a gentle lift, not a deep backbend.

safeAsanas.name: Bhujangasana, mini/Sphinx variant only
safeAsanas.note: Small, gentle extension only — not the full deep cobra.

safeAsanas.name: Pawanmuktasana, gentle single-leg
safeAsanas.note: One knee to chest at a time, gently — avoid pulling both knees in hard.

halfOrModifiedOnly.name: Ustrasana (Camel pose)
halfOrModifiedOnly.note: Jindal's own sheet marks this half-only — shallow backbend, hands on hips or lower back, not full reach to heels.

halfOrModifiedOnly.name: Shalabhasana (Locust pose)
halfOrModifiedOnly.note: Jindal's own sheet marks this half-only — lift one leg at a time gently, not both legs with full chest lift.

avoidAsanas.name: Surya Namaskar (full sequence)
avoidAsanas.note: Crossed out on Jindal's own sheet — the forward-fold/lunge/backbend sequence loads the lumbar spine repeatedly.

avoidAsanas.name: Naukasana (Boat pose)
avoidAsanas.note: Crossed out on Jindal's own sheet — strong abdominal/hip-flexor loading compresses the lower spine.

avoidAsanas.name: Halasana (Plough pose)
avoidAsanas.note: Deep spinal flexion under load — avoid.

avoidAsanas.name: Sarvangasana (Shoulder stand)
avoidAsanas.note: Inverted spinal load — avoid without specific clearance.

avoidAsanas.name: Paschimottanasana (deep seated forward fold)
avoidAsanas.note: Deep forward flexion — avoid the full pose; a gentle hamstring stretch with a soft spine is fine instead.

avoidAsanas.name: Chakrasana / full Dhanurasana (Wheel / full Bow)
avoidAsanas.note: Full backbends — avoid without physio clearance.

spinalYoga.note: Ask the Highgate physio to confirm this list directly — it's built from Jindal's own annotations plus general spondylolisthesis guidance, not a personalised physio assessment.

zumba.detail: Standard Zumba involves jumping, rapid direction changes and twisting under momentum — exactly the loaded-twist / high-impact combination generally cautioned against with a bilateral pars defect. A low-impact format (often branded 'Zumba Gold' or a studio's 'low-impact' class) keeps the cardio and the fun without the jumping/twisting load. Ask the Highgate physio to confirm before doing a full-intensity class; start with low-impact only.

spinning.detail: Stationary cycling is low-impact and commonly recommended for spondylolisthesis, but posture matters: get the saddle height/position set so you're not hunched forward, keep the core gently braced, and avoid heavy-resistance standing climbs (they load the lumbar spine through the hips). A seated, moderate-resistance spin class is a solid cardio option once cleared for exercise.

walkRun.title: Walking → running progression

phases.name: Phase 1 — Recovery (now, through October)
phases.detail: Gentle daily walking only, built into the commute + deliberate walk blocks above. No running. Focus: hydration + consistency, not pace or distance.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Post-clearance build-up (from doctor + physio sign-off, ~mid-Nov)
phases.detail: Brisk walking, building duration before intensity — e.g. extend the weekend walk toward 45-60 min before introducing any jogging.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Walk-run intervals (physio-gated)
phases.detail: Short jogging intervals inside a walk (e.g. 1 min jog / 2 min walk, building gradually) only once the physio has specifically assessed the back for impact tolerance — ask this at the Highgate session.

phases.name: Phase 4 — 5K prep restart (physio-gated)
phases.detail: Resume the earlier-2026 5K training programme only after Phase 3 is tolerated without back symptoms. Bring the old programme to the physio session to sanity-check the jump in weekly mileage.

walkRun.note: Every phase transition is physio/doctor-gated, not date-gated — move to the next phase when cleared, not on a calendar.

trainerFocus.title: What to focus on once trainer sessions resume

areas.title: Core stability, not core flexion
areas.detail: Bird-dog, dead bug, Pallof press, planks (modified as needed) — brace-and-hold work rather than crunches/sit-ups, which load the spine in the direction spondylolisthesis is most vulnerable to.

areas.title: Posterior chain / glute strengthening
areas.detail: Glute bridges, hip thrusts, clamshells — weak glutes are commonly implicated in spondylolisthesis-related back strain, so this is a high-value focus area.

areas.title: Avoid axial spinal loading
areas.detail: Skip loaded back squats/deadlifts with spinal flexion initially — prefer goblet squats, leg press, supported rows, chest press. Reintroduce heavier axial loading only with physio sign-off.

areas.title: Wrist/grip strength
areas.detail: Continues the thera clay + light dumbbell work already underway — progressive, little and often.

areas.title: General conditioning for weight loss
areas.detail: Moderate-intensity circuits/intervals (bike, rower, walking incline) rather than high-impact plyometrics — supports the 500-750 kcal/day deficit without adding injury risk.

areas.title: Posture
areas.detail: Given the L5-S1 pars defect and long desk/commute hours, posture cueing (neutral pelvis, avoiding prolonged flexion) is worth a standing agenda item in every session.

dietBooklet.intro: A browsable set of options — not a rigid single menu — weaving together BAUS (primary authority for stone safety), Jindal Naturecure, and the food logic from 'Luke's diet', filtered to what you actually like and what's realistic for a weekday office lunch. Tap/click any item for the reasoning.

items.name: Aldi muesli with milk or curd
items.detail: Your regular — fine as an everyday choice. Curd instead of milk adds a calcium hit that pairs well with the day's oxalate intake (BAUS).

items.name: Fruit + curd
items.detail: Quick, hits BAUS's 'well-balanced, not too many calories' principle, and the curd covers the calcium-pairing point.

items.name: Homemade paratha + curd
items.detail: Homemade (not shop-bought/frozen) keeps salt and processed fat down versus the 'sneaky' pre-made versions you flagged. Curd alongside is the calcium pairing.

items.name: Dosa/idli + sambar (wife's home-made)
items.detail: Fermented batter is gentle on digestion (Jindal principle); sambar's lentils add protein and fibre, which helps blunt the post-meal glucose rise given the prediabetic HbA1c.

items.name: Ragi Dosa / Idli
items.detail: From the Jindal recipe batch — fits the stone/liver/sugar checks (section C3 of your tracker) and is a reasonable rotation option alongside the usual dosa.

items.name: Oats Porridge
items.detail: Appears in both the Jindal material and Luke's diet — fibre-forward, helps the fatty-liver and glucose picture.

items.name: Occasional: M&S dark-chocolate protein cereal
items.detail: Fine occasionally, not as the daily default — cocoa is a moderate-oxalate item and it's higher in sugar than the everyday options above.

items.name: Big mixed salad + paneer
items.detail: Lettuce/cucumber/pepper base (not spinach-heavy), paneer for protein + calcium, olive oil-lemon dressing — the lemon also supports BAUS's citrate/less-acidic-urine advice.

items.name: Big mixed salad + kala chana or tofu
items.detail: Same base, swap protein for variety across the week.

items.name: Vegetable soup + sourdough slice
items.detail: Good option on a cold or lower-appetite day — sourdough is on your favourites list and easier to digest than some other breads.

items.name: Quinoa salad bowl
items.detail: Higher protein/fibre than a plain salad, still realistic to buy or bring in.

items.name: Rajma + rice/roti + curd
items.detail: Kidney beans are a moderate-oxalate item, fine in a normal portion, especially paired with the curd's calcium.

items.name: Kala chana + roti + curd
items.detail: Same logic as rajma — favourite, moderate oxalate, calcium-paired.

items.name: Dal makhani + rice, moderate portion + curd
items.detail: You like this a lot — keep portion moderate given the butter/cream content, for the fatty-liver and weight goals rather than the stone risk.

items.name: Kali dal + roti + curd
items.detail: Same as dal makhani — moderate portion for the liver/weight goals.

items.name: Bhindi (okra) sabzi + roti
items.detail: Okra is a moderate-oxalate item per BAUS — fine in sensible portions, no need to exclude.

items.name: Karela sabzi + roti
items.detail: You like it, and it's not flagged on any oxalate list — freely fine.

items.name: Saag paneer, moderate spinach portion
items.detail: Spinach is on BAUS's avoid list, but pairing it with paneer's calcium in the same dish binds much of the oxalate before it reaches the kidneys — the trade-off is keeping this occasional and the spinach portion moderate, not the everyday spinach-heavy version.

items.name: Khichdi
items.detail: Gentle, easy-digestion option from both Jindal and Luke's diet — good for a lighter evening.

items.name: Channa Dal Cabbage Curry
items.detail: Fits the stone/liver/sugar fit-check in your tracker (section C3).

items.name: Beans and Corn Subzi / Makai Capsicum White Sauce / Mushroom with Dhania
items.detail: All checked fine against BAUS — good rotation options for variety.

items.name: Fruit (apple, banana, berries, oranges)
items.detail: Whole fruit is the preferred vitamin-C source over supplements (BAUS caution on high-dose vitamin C supplements).

items.name: Curd / buttermilk
items.detail: Calcium top-up throughout the day, not just at meals.

items.name: Roasted chana
items.detail: A savoury-crunch swap for the chip habit that still fits the diet.

items.name: Coconut water, lemon water, barley water
items.detail: All on the 'fine to use now' drinks list — support hydration target and citrate.

items.name: Occasional: Lay's kettle chips (salted)
items.detail: Fine as an occasional treat, not the nightly default — salt content works against both the stone-prevention salt target and the cholesterol/HDL ratio.

items.name: Occasional: dark chocolate square
items.detail: Cocoa is moderate-oxalate and adds sugar — a square now and then is fine, daily isn't the target.

items.name: Occasional: avocado toast (Farmer J)
items.detail: Nutritionally fine in itself — keep it occasional mainly for the overall calorie/weight-loss budget.

items.name: Ghiya / bottle gourd
items.detail: You dislike it regardless — no loss. Also note the tracker's safety flag: if any ghiya juice tastes bitter, don't drink it — can cause serious illness.

items.name: Almond milk / almonds / cashews
items.detail: High-oxalate nuts — you're not a fan of almond milk anyway, so this is an easy one to actually stick to.

items.name: Beetroot, rhubarb, celery
items.detail: BAUS avoid list — you're also not a big beetroot fan, so little is lost.

items.name: Wheat bran
items.detail: High-oxalate despite being high-fibre — BAUS specifically calls this out.

items.name: Shop-bought/frozen parathas & chips as a nightly habit
items.detail: The 'sneaky' night snacks you flagged yourself — swap for homemade versions or fruit/curd most nights, keep as an occasional exception.

tips: BAUS guidance: aim for 2.5-3L fluid daily, spread evenly, with an extra glass alongside each meal — dilute urine reduces stone-forming crystals.

Calcium isn't the enemy: BAUS advises keeping normal dietary calcium (dairy, paneer) rather than cutting it — pairing calcium with oxalate-rich food actually binds oxalate in the gut before it reaches your kidneys.
High-oxalate foods to keep occasional, not daily: spinach, rhubarb, beetroot, almonds/cashews, bran, cocoa/dark chocolate, strong tea.
Jindal principle: warm water with a squeeze of lime before breakfast supports digestion.
For L5-S1 spondylolisthesis: avoid deep forward spinal flexion and heavy twisting loads — core stability work (bird-dog, dead bug, glute bridge) protects the joint better than sit-ups.
Sitting numbness check: if you've been at your desk over 45 minutes, stand and move for 2 minutes — prolonged static sitting triggers the sciatic numbness, not activity itself.
Anulom Vilom, Bhramari and Ujjayi breathing (Jindal routine) work well as a 10-minute wind-down — helps sleep and lowers stress-driven cortisol, which also supports blood sugar control.
Prediabetic HbA1c of 39: pairing carbs with protein/fibre (roti with dal, not roti alone) blunts the glucose spike more than cutting carbs entirely.
Fatty liver, ALT already improving (67 to 45): keep added sugar and saturated fat down, and keep the walking consistent — daily movement is one of the few proven ways to reduce liver fat.
Sustainable pace beats speed: 0.5-1kg/week is the range least likely to rebound — matches your own goal of not yo-yo'ing back up.
Vitamin C caution (BAUS): keep supplemental vitamin C modest — high-dose supplements convert to oxalate. Get vitamin C from whole fruit instead (oranges, berries), where the effect is different.
Eye yoga day: palming, focus shifts and blinking exercises help offset a screen-heavy day.
Wrist strength: light dumbbells + the level-4 thera clay squeeze build grip gradually — little and often beats one heavy session.
Jal neti (twice weekly): use lukewarm saline, never plain tap water, and finish with gentle nose-blowing to clear residual solution.
15k steps: your Archway-Canary Wharf-Highgate commute already covers a big chunk — the PM Highgate-to-home leg and lunchtime movement are usually where the gap closes or doesn't.
Spinning is generally a good low-impact cardio option for L5-S1 once cleared — just watch saddle position and skip heavy-resistance standing climbs.
Zumba: go for a low-impact/'Gold'-style class rather than full-intensity — the jumping and twisting in standard Zumba is the exact combination to be cautious about with a pars defect.
